title: Void Ending in a Square to Venus
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The square is one of the two worst aspects in the lunar doctrine, an enmity the text grades as moderate because the signs it joins stand two natures apart. The counsel that guards every election runs exactly here: watch the square and the opposition in everything, and keep the Moon from the unfortunate planets in these figures above all.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a square to Venus, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of her sweetness and her song. Venus governs taste, the text says, and with it beauty and love: poetic meter, songs, dancing, painting, and perfumes fall to her, with places of music and merriment among her locations. She is the Lesser Fortune, and her benevolence fits the works of youths, pleasures, and women. Pearls are her stones, the sweet smells are hers, and her colors are sky blue and gold fading into green.
